tools.name: publish_page
tools.description: Publish text or markdown as a clean, shareable public web page and get back a URL you can hand to a human. Use this whenever you produce a report, summary, plan, table, or any result a person should read in a browser instead of the chat window. To keep ONE page updated across runs/sessions, pass a s

tools.name: update_page
tools.description: Update the title and/or content of a page you previously published; the URL never changes. Use this to keep one stable link current across sessions or runs — a live status page, a running changelog, an append-as-you-go log, or a dashboard the recipient can bookmark once and always see fresh.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List the pages you have published, newest first, with their URLs and view counts.

tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: Delete a page you published, by id.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "update_page" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "{key}" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: publish_page, list_pages · Public sink: publish_page · Destructive: delete_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: publish_page, list_pages · Public sink: publish_page · Destructive: delete_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
